default.description: Core permissions for the Nibbin desktop shell. Grants the main app webview the event plugin (listen/emit) so native→UI signals work — e.g. the C6 hotkey-pause re-render (study:paused-by-hotkey) and the sign-out re-boot. Scoped to the local main webview only; the embedded Grove webview loads remote content and is not listed (no `remote` field), so it gets no Tauri permissions.

grove-remote.description: Scoped IPC capability for the embedded nibbin.com Grove webview. Grants the full thin-shell bridge command set to content loaded from https://nibbin.com. Security model: (a) targets the 'grove' webview label only — not the 'main' webview; (b) sets local:false so local app content cannot use this capability; (c) uses an exact-origin URLPattern (no wildcard subdomains) matching the production and NIBBIN_GROVE_HANDOFF origins. The on_navigation lock in lib.rs (grove_show ~line 91) provides defense-in-depth by blocking same-webview navigation to any other host. Together these two layers ensure no other origin — including attacker-controlled redirects — can reach these commands. Write/control commands (send_control, create_study, review_delete, review_keep, add_exclusion, remove_exclusion) are included because the two-layer containment model makes the nibbin.com webview a trusted origin equivalent to the native desktop UI; the daemon remains the sole enforcer of C2/C3/C4/C5. Full rationale in bridge-read.toml.
